reasons: The rule's expected exit clause is genuinely absent: Section 14 only continues services to the end of the month following notice, and Section 13 places the burden of finding a new name server/hosting entirely on Client while imposing no vendor obligation to return, export or delete Client Content or Credit Data — so neither the preferred nor the 90-day/30-day fallback is met.

The insert is actionable and tracks the model language (six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, deletion plus written certification), correctly mapped to the parties' defined names (TrueLink/Client) and to the document's own data terms (Client Content, Credit Data, Web Site).

Placement in Section 14 (Termination) follows the redline guidance and is effective post-termination given the Section 24 survival of Sections 5–30; the original paragraph text is left intact, so the edit is minimal (insertion only).

Comment is accurate, in the required voice and prefix, explains the change and the rationale, and offers the 90-day fallback without lecturing; deterministic checks confirm data-return/transition language is present in the redline.
